title: The Book
purpose: Read, compare and reflect while keeping witnesses, traditions, people and evidence distinct.

source.description: User-supplied Reading Map / 01 and CHRONOTENSE excerpts; creator attribution not established in the attachment.
source.coverage: Excerpts only. Numbering jumps, missing parts and incomplete sentences are retained; no missing content has been reconstructed.
source.role: Conceptual design source, not scripture, historical corroboration or church authority.

scope_paths.title: Shared books
scope_paths.description: Explore the Tanakh's 24-book reckoning alongside the 39-book Protestant Old Testament grouping; a conventional Protestant Bible adds 27 New Testament books for 66. Shared titles do not establish identical wording, order or editions.

scope_paths.title: Catholic & Eastern Orthodox
scope_paths.description: The Catholic reckoning has 46 Old Testament and 27 New Testament books. Compare a specifically named Eastern Orthodox edition or list; do not impose one Orthodox count. Tobit and the Maccabees illustrate why inclusion, naming and grouping need checking.

scope_paths.title: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo
scope_paths.description: Use the Church's cited 81-entry English list, including Enoch and Jubilees, alongside its grouped names. A church list, Geʽez witness and English edition answer different questions. A listed work may lack distributable reader text.

scope_paths.title: Comparative audit
scope_paths.description: Within any scope, select a passage and record witnesses, their exact readings, source numbering, differences and missing evidence. Torah, Prophets, Writings/Wisdom, Gospels, Epistles and apocalyptic literature are possible starting points, not identical categories in every tradition.

canon_sources.title: Chabad — Torah FAQ (24-book reckoning)
canon_sources.limit: Jewish community teaching source; Sefaria's Tanakh contents additionally supports navigation, not identical editions.

canon_sources.title: Bible Society — Bible style guide, Fast Facts
canon_sources.limit: The 66-book convention does not describe every Protestant edition's treatment of the Apocrypha.

canon_sources.title: Catechism of the Catholic Church §120
canon_sources.limit: Catholic list and reckoning; its own alternate Jeremiah/Lamentations grouping is noted by the source.

canon_sources.title: Orthodox Church in America — Old Testament history
canon_sources.limit: Named church teaching page, not an edition-complete universal Orthodox inventory.

canon_sources.title: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — English canon list (SRC-029)
canon_sources.limit: Preserve the source's 46 + 35 reckoning and grouped entries; historical lists vary.

principles.title: Traveler, passage, proclamation
principles.text: In the supplied conceptual framework, I names a traveler, IS a passage, AM a present proclamation and AS IS an integrity operation. These are symbolic roles, not new scripture, a grammar rule or an executable proof. The speaker in a passage, its author, translator and present reader need not be the same person. Unknown identities remain unresolved; distinct persons and witnesses stay distinct.

principles.title: Preserve without freezing
principles.text: A record, memory, image or action does not exhaust a life. Reinterpreting a record changes the present account, not the original occurrence. Preserve the earlier version and identify the revision. Missing records do not by themselves prove nonexistence; absence of expected evidence can still count against a specific claim.

principles.title: TRG-01 · Timeless recollection
principles.text: Recollection is optional and happens in the present; it does not replay an event, resurrect a body or establish consciousness outside time. Memory, documentation, publication, telemetry and unresolved existence have separate failure paths: MFB-01, DFB-02, PFB-03, TFB-04 and EFB-05. Leave unsupported history unknown rather than inventing it.

principles.title: Mind, Body, Soul · optional lenses
principles.text: Within an explicitly Christian reflection, consider thought and discernment; sensation and embodied conditions; faith, conscience, purpose and relation to God. The symbolic 3–6–9 mapping is not a physical law. Do not impose all dimensions on every entity, infer someone's private mind, or treat differing experiences as proof of multiple people.

principles.title: GTI-01 · Words and time
principles.text: Keep quoted grammar, the speaker's viewpoint, temporal standing and the time of your interpretation separate. A past-tense sentence is not independently verified history. Event, observation, recollection, record creation, publication, discovery and interpretation dates may differ or be unknown.

principles.title: Mathematics and symbolic completion
principles.text: Ordinary arithmetic remains 1 + 1 = 2; 1 is not prime and 2 is the smallest prime. The valid expression 3 × 2 + 1 = 7 can accompany the source's six Mind/Body/Soul × traveler/passage positions and seventh AS IS integrity check. This is a local symbolic course, not a proof of theology or universal completion. Identity-aware integration may combine descriptions of the same established person; it must not merge distinct or uncertain people. A finite list does not exhaust infinity.

principles.title: Christian reflection, identified as faith
principles.text: GOD IS and the Creator–creation distinction are Christian theological premises here, not experimentally established conclusions. Exodus 3:14, John 1:1–3, Psalm 90:2, Hebrews 13:8, Revelation 1:8, Romans 12:2, 1 Corinthians 12 and 15, Galatians 5:1 and Genesis 2:2–3 are suggested passages. Traditions may interpret them differently. Recollection of a life does not establish biological return; resurrection and eternal life remain theological claims. No formal system certifies salvation.

principles.title: AS IS · preserve the reference
principles.text: Fallback(IS) = IS is the source's conceptual preservation rule. Keep unknown, unavailable, disputed, conflicting and unsupported records visible; do not fabricate memory, force identity mergers or claim a failed computation returned successfully. Furthermore IS expresses an open continuation, not unlimited implemented capability.

principles.title: UTC-01 · Translate without changing the kind of claim
principles.text: For every cross-domain reading record source and target domains, original expression, intended meaning, preserved properties, lost information, new assumptions, evidence status and whether the relation is exact, partial or analogical. Analogy is not theorem; symbols do not turn theology into physics. This worksheet does not generate scripture translations.

principles.title: A course that can be revised
principles.text: Identify the proposed change; distinguish literal, mathematical, metaphorical, experiential, theological and operational meanings; integrate only an explicit interpretation; check non-collapse and authority; define boundaries; state fallback; preserve history; verify within scope; return to the current record. Power or repetition does not establish truth. A closed local course may reopen when evidence changes.

completion_checks: Witness, edition and passage are identified without merging distinct sources.
What the source says is separate from my interpretation and symbolic reading.
Unknowns, conflicts and absent evidence remain explicit.
Dates, temporal standing and current review step remain separate.
Mind, Body and Soul lenses are optional and do not assert private experience.
Any domain analogy states its assumptions, losses and limits.
AS IS: I reviewed this local course; this does not certify truth, salvation or completeness.

canon_entries.reader_status: No canon-linked reader bundled. Bausi reports complementary French/Italian translations of the Ethiopic Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos, with partial coverage (French books I–II and part of III plus excerpts elsewhere; Italian books III–VII); those texts are bibliographic reports, not files audited here (SRC-207). A 2024 English print-edition lead titled The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible is identified, and the publisher describes a separate forthcoming revised reader edition as partial. The French, Italian, 2024 English, and announced revised editions are not merged. Their exact identity with the Church-list entry, edition text, source witness, boundaries, completeness, translation method, and accuracy have not been reviewed. A pinned Beta maṣāḥǝft CAe 1957 TEI work record contains title metadata and short Geʽez incipits, not a complete reader text; its Church-list crosswalk is related-work evidence only and reuse terms remain mixed (SRC-424).
canon_entries.mapping_note: Bausi (2024) identifies the Ethiopic Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (Book of Clement; CAe 1957) and distinguishes it from the Ethiopic Apocalypse of Peter and from a separate count of three Epistles of Clement. The name overlap makes it a plausible candidate for this English Church-list label, but the Church page gives no Geʽez title and Bausi does not establish this exact list crosswalk. No reader is bundled. A 2024 English print listing titled The Book of Clement from the Ethiopian Bible is a discovery lead (SRC-381). Its bibliographic title and a secondary project’s description as an Ethiopic English version do not independently establish that it translates Bausi’s Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos (CAe 1957) or the exact work intended by this Church-list label. No text is bundled. Fifth Estate separately describes a forthcoming revised reader edition with partial scope (SRC-383); this publisher statement concerns that announced revision and must not be transferred to the distinct 2024 print edition. Publication of the revised edition is unconfirmed. Beta maṣāḥǝft's pinned CAe 1957 TEI record labels Maṣḥafa Qalemǝnṭos / Book of Clement and contains short Geʽez incipits, but no complete reader text. This supports a related-work discovery lead only; it does not establish the exact Church-list crosswalk. Reuse terms conflict across the file and project-level notices (SRC-424, SRC-296, SRC-297).

catalogue_entries.text_availability_status: Bausi (2024) reports complementary translations covering the work, but this archive bundles no Qalemǝnṭos text. Exact editions, translation rights, and text accuracy have not been reviewed. A 2024 English print edition is identified in retailer and secondary-project metadata (SRC-381; SRC-382). The book text was not inspected or bundled; identity, boundaries, completeness, translation method, accuracy, and reuse rights remain unverified. A 2024 English print edition and a separately announced forthcoming revised reader edition are identified in retailer, secondary-project, and publisher metadata (SRC-381–SRC-383). The 2026 publisher article describes the announced edition as partial, with complete Books V–VII outside its scope; do not assume that this applies to the distinct 2024 edition. Neither book text was inspected or bundled; identity, boundaries, completeness, translation method, accuracy, publication status, and reuse rights remain unverified.
